purpose: Separate initialized GPU/MPS-client lifecycle effects from socket/process retirement and clean-PUSCH input effects after Confirm39 sham deadline misses. The MPS worker runs ten pre-ready GPU warmup units but zero units during the timed RAN epoch; the CPU worker never creates a CUDA context.

execution.operational_requalification: 200 conventional-only P60/D35 releases with zero misses

interpretation_limit: Use each seed/order pair as one unit for an exact one-sided sign test; releases within a round may share a timing disturbance. The contrast bundles GPU warmup, CUDA context creation, MPS registration and retirement; it cannot isolate which substep causes a tail. A significant MPS excess under this clean-PUSCH D35 harness supports a GPU-client-lifecycle-linked timing mechanism, not universal causality. A nonsignificant result is inconclusive, not evidence of safety. No frozen threshold is revised after seeing data.
